issues.description: setuptools<82 cap leaked into runtime install_requires in core/setup.py instead of being scoped to CI/build
issues.detail: The setuptools<82 pin is a build-time workaround for mmcv/mmengine still importing pkg_resources, which setuptools 82 removed. Adding it to core/setup.py's install_requires/extras propagates this transient CI constraint to every downstream consumer of autogluon.core forever. setuptools is a build tool, not a runtime dependency — the constraint belongs in the CI scripts (which already have it) or a build-only constraints file, not in published package metadata. Either justify the runtime need explicitly or remove it from core/setup.py.

issues.description: core/setup.py pin lacks a FIXME breadcrumb and termination criterion linking it to mmcv#3325
issues.detail: env_setup.sh and setup_mmcv.sh carry FIXME comments pointing at the upstream mmcv issue, but core/setup.py has no comment at all explaining why setuptools is capped. When mmcv#3325 is resolved, a maintainer has to grep three files to find and remove this workaround, and the core/setup.py site has no breadcrumb at all. Add a comment at every pin site pointing to the upstream issue and stating the precise condition under which the cap may be lifted (e.g., a shared MMCV_3325_WORKAROUND tag).

issues.description: mmcv installed with --no-build-isolation introduces an undocumented ordering/environment coupling
issues.detail: Switching from `mim install mmcv` to `pip install mmcv==2.1.0 --no-build-isolation` means mmcv now builds against the ambient environment's setuptools/torch/CUDA rather than an isolated build env. The setuptools<82 pin must already be installed before this line runs, and the script is now silently sensitive to reordering. Add a comment stating the ordering invariant (setuptools<82 must hold throughout the install sequence) and the rationale for abandoning mim, so a future cleanup doesn't break the build.

issues.description: mmdet bumped 3.2.0 -> 3.3.0 with no stated rationale
issues.detail: The PR is framed as 'fix mmengine failure' but also bundles an mmdet version bump. Either the bump is required by mmengine 0.10.7 / mmcv 2.1.0 compatibility (state it in a comment) or it is unrelated drift (drop it from this PR). As-is, a future bisect cannot separate the mmdet bump from the setuptools cap or the mmengine source change.

issues.description: Duplicate setuptools<82 pin in three files with no single source of truth
issues.detail: The same cap now lives in env_setup.sh, setup_mmcv.sh, and core/setup.py. When the upstream fix lands, all three sites must be reverted in sync, and partial reversion will leave a silent residual constraint. Consolidate to a single source of truth (shared variable, single script, or one tagged location) so the cleanup is mechanical rather than archaeological.

issues.description: mmengine swap from git SHA to PyPI 0.10.7 drops the torch 2.5 fix rationale
issues.detail: The prior install used a specific mmengine git SHA chosen because it contained the fix for torch 2.5. The new install pins mmengine==0.10.7 from PyPI with no comment confirming that 0.10.7 contains the same torch 2.5 fix. Add a one-line note confirming the compatibility postcondition is preserved, otherwise the torch 2.5 contract is now weaker than before with no breadcrumb.

issues.description: Empty PR description on a multi-change CI workaround
issues.detail: The PR body contains no statement of the problem, the reasoning, or the exit criteria for the workaround. For a change that pins a major build tool, switches an install method, and bumps a related package, the description should state the failure signature, the upstream issue link, the rationale for each bundled change, and the condition under which the FIXMEs can be removed.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges strongly: the CI fix itself is a reasonable triage for the setuptools 82 / pkg_resources removal that broke mmcv/mmengine builds, and the FIXME pointers to mmcv#3325 in the workflow scripts are well-placed. The unanimous P1 concern is that the setuptools<82 cap leaked from CI into core/setup.py's runtime install_requires, exporting a transient build-time workaround as a permanent constraint on every downstream user — and worse, that site has no FIXME breadcrumb tying it to the upstream issue. Secondary issues bundled into the same diff (unexplained mmdet 3.2.0->3.3.0 bump, switch from mim to pip --no-build-isolation without documenting the new ordering coupling, mmengine git-SHA to PyPI wheel swap without confirming the torch 2.5 fix is preserved, triplicated pin with no single source of truth, and an empty PR body) make future bisection and cleanup harder. Recommended action: pull the setuptools pin out of core/setup.py (or justify it as a runtime need), add FIXME/termination comments at every remaining pin site, and explain the mmdet bump and the mim->pip switch in the PR description before landing.
